request.input:
You repair a Boolean network model of the DNA damage response (a published model, Gupta et al. 2023).
A claim read from the literature was turned into a rule change by a fixed template, and an exact solver rejected the
change: the edited network contradicts behaviours the model must keep (the verification cases). Propose another rule
for the node that still expresses the claim but passes those cases.

Rules are written with node names and the operators ! (not), & (and), | (or) and parentheses. A node is 1 when active.
DNA_damage is the only input. These are the nodes you may use: AKT, AMPK_MAPK, ATM_pH2AX, ATR, BAX, BCL2, CHK2, Caspase, Cdc25, Cdc2_CycB, DNA_PK, DNA_damage, E2F1, Mdm2, Myc, PTEN, PUMA, RB, Sirt1, TUG1, ULK1_Beclin1, WWP1, Wee1, Wip1, hTERT, mTORC1, mTORC2, miR221, p21, p53, p53_A, p53_INP1, p53_K

CLAIM: DNA_PK activates ATM_pH2AX   (3 paper(s))
EVIDENCE:
- PMC3461360 (in MNNG-treated cells, pharmacological and gene knockout experiments): "Employing a pharmacological approach and gene knockout cells, we also demonstrate in this paper that the phosphatidylinositol-3-OH kinase-related kinases (PIKKs) ATM (ataxia telangiectasia mutated) and DNA-dependent protein kinase (DNA-PK) mediate γH2AX generation and, consequently, MNNG-induced necroptosis."
- PMC6547644 (review statement, DNA-PKcs-deficient cells): "Expression of ATM is regulated by DNA-PKcs such that ATM protein levels are decreased in DNA-PKcs-deficient cells72."
- PMC6990542 (ATM-deficient or inhibited cells, residual IR-induced phosphorylation): "also contribute to the residual IR induced phosphorylation of ATM substrates (e.g., H2AX, SMC1 and KAP1) in ATM-deficient or inhibited cells [20, 30, 31]"

NODE TO CHANGE: ATM_pH2AX
CURRENT RULE:   ATM_pH2AX, (DNA_damage & (!Wip1 | !Cdc25 | E2F1)) | (ATR & DNA_damage & TUG1 & !miR221)
TEMPLATE RULE (rejected): ATM_pH2AX, ((DNA_damage & (!Wip1 | !Cdc25 | E2F1)) | (ATR & DNA_damage & TUG1 & !miR221)) | DNA_PK

WHY IT WAS REJECTED (counterexamples from the solver; "setting" fixes nodes to 0 or 1, a phenotype is read from the
fixed points; the witness is a fixed point of the edited network):
- the rule passes every verification case but changes no fixed point in any scenario tested (wild type with and without damage, and the nodes of the claim and of the rule each switched off and on): the condition you added is never met where it matters, so the claim is expressed in name only. Choose a condition that is met in at least one such scenario.

EARLIER ATTEMPTS THAT ALSO FAILED:
- (DNA_damage & (!Wip1 | !Cdc25 | E2F1)) | (ATR & DNA_damage & TUG1 & !miR221) | (DNA_PK & DNA_damage & TUG1 & !miR221)  ->  ['vacuous']: the rule passes every verification case but changes no fixed point in any scenario tested (wild type with and without damage, and the nodes of the claim and of the rule each switched off and on): the condition you added is never met where it matters, so the claim is expressed in name only. Choose a 
- (DNA_damage & (!Wip1 | !Cdc25 | E2F1)) | (ATR & DNA_damage & TUG1 & !miR221) | ((DNA_PK | ATR) & DNA_damage & !miR221 & !Caspase)  ->  ['vacuous']: the rule passes every verification case but changes no fixed point in any scenario tested (wild type with and without damage, and the nodes of the claim and of the rule each switched off and on): the condition you added is never met where it matters, so the claim is expressed in name only. Choose a 

Requirements, all checked by the solver afterwards:
- DNA_PK must be able to switch ATM_pH2AX on and never off: it acts on ATM_pH2AX only in the direction 'activates'.
- Keep every influence the current rule has: every node in the current rule must still affect the new rule in the same way.
- The rule must change at least one prediction. If you only restore the cases by gating the new term with a condition that
  is never true where it matters (for example a node that is always on or off whenever the term could act), the solver
  rejects it as vacuous. The condition should be one under which the claimed effect actually shows.
- Use only the nodes listed above. Do not use ATM_pH2AX in its own rule.
- You may restrict WHEN the claimed effect applies by combining it with other nodes, if the evidence context (cell
  type, condition) or the counterexample suggests a condition. Say which condition you chose and why. Do not invent a
  mechanism the evidence does not support.
- If no rule can both express the claim and pass the cases, set give_up to true and explain.

Answer as JSON: {"rule": "<expression only, no node name and no comma>", "explanation": "...", "give_up": false}.

text: {"explanation": "I condition the new DNA-PK input on low CHK2 signaling. CHK2 is the principal downstream kinase of ATM, so !CHK2 marks the ATM-deficient/inhibited context in PMC6990542, where DNA-PK provides residual phosphorylation of ATM substrates including H2AX. In the CHK2-off scenario Cdc25 is derepressed and the original ATM_pH2AX terms can switch off, so the DNA-PK term is actually exercised and changes a fixed point, rather than being vacuous. DNA_PK appears only positively, and all original terms and influences are retained unchanged.", "give_up": false, "rule": "(DNA_damage & (!Wip1 | !Cdc25 | E2F1)) | (ATR & DNA_damage & TUG1 & !miR221) | (DNA_PK & DNA_damage & !CHK2)"}
